3.2. Counting direction-consistent circuits: generalized BEST theorem. The well-known BEST theorem, named after de Bruijn and van Aardenne-Ehrenfest [vAEdB51] and Smith and Tutte [TS41], provides an efficient algorithm of counting Eulerian cycles on an Eulerian digraph Go(meaning that the in-degree and out-degree at each vertex of Goare identical). Denote by ec(G, o) the number of Eulerian cycles on G, and In (G, o) the number of arborescences ∏ G rooted at w. Then the BEST theorem states that ec(G, o) = In (G, o) · (deg (v) − 1)! where deg (v) is the out-degree of G at v ∈ V (G). Note that by a directed version of Kirchhoff’s matrix-tree theorem, In (G, o) is actually independent of w, and can be efficiently computed as the determinant of the reduced Laplacian matrix L (G). Before making a generalization of the BEST theorem, we first introduce a notion of weighted Laplacian here.
